data.narrative:
Red 6, a Series B+ stage defense and security company that has raised over $100M, operates within a sector containing 23 identifiable peers—2 public and 8 private entities tracked. The identifiable public comparables are DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS. Notable private peers in adjacent segments include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable to this analysis. The Defense & Security sector, while populated, lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with analogous valuation tiers. Filtering across stage and scale produced fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for meaningful triangulation. A sector-wide median would obscure material differences in funding stage, technology maturity, and addressable market positioning. Consequently, traditional comparable-company analysis cannot be reliably anchored.

The lack of tight peer clustering creates material valuation uncertainty for Red 6. Without statistically robust comparables at matching stage and scale, any valuation range would rest heavily on methodology beyond peer multiples—namely discounted cash flow assumptions, revenue growth projections, or market sizing—none of which are provided in the available data. For Series B+ stage companies in defense tech, this scarcity of true peers reflects the sector's fragmentation and nascency. A credible valuation would require either: (1) deep-dive analysis of the public and private comps despite stage mismatches, or (2) primary research into Red 6's unit economics, customer concentration, and competitive positioning.
